page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor built on the ARMv9 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 33 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8gb.4xlarge demonstrates strong memory subsystem performance, achieving a top-tier rating in the PassMark memory score and strong results in uncached large-block memory bandwidth, with reads at 294.53 GB/sec and writes at 132.58 GB/sec. CPU-bound tasks show average performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong at 202.01 GB/sec, while database operations score a strong 24174.88 in PassMark. However, LLM inference performance is mixed, with medium 7B model prompt processing rated as weak at 31.06 tokens/sec, though text generation remains average at 17.45 tokens/sec.

This server offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound workloads that benefit from dedicated ARMv9 physical cores without hyperthreading overhead. The absence of local NVMe storage and GPUs makes it less suitable for heavy storage-bound databases or deep learning training. It is best suited for multi-threaded CPU tasks, high-throughput web serving, memory-bandwidth-sensitive operations, and compiled software development.
